cues: The testes hang in the scrotum, two degrees cooler than the body, because sperm cannot be made at body temperature.
Seminiferous tubules make sperm; the Leydig cells between them make testosterone.
Sperm mature in the epididymis and travel through the vas deferens, joined by fluid from the seminal vesicles, rich in fructose for energy, and from the prostate.
text: The male system. The testes hang in the scrotum, two degrees cooler than the body, because sperm cannot be made at body temperature. Seminiferous tubules make sperm; the Leydig cells between them make testosterone. Sperm mature in the epididymis and travel through the vas deferens, joined by fluid from the seminal vesicles, rich in fructose for energy, and from the prostate.
